data.narrative:
Retro Biosciences, a Series A-stage biotech company founded by Joe Betts-LaCroix, is evaluated against a comp universe of 3 public peers (RXRX, TEM, ONT.L) and 8 private biotech firms in the Biotech & Health sector, including Colossal Biosciences, Chai Discovery, and Recursion Pharmaceuticals.

Stage-progression methodology is the primary applicable technique given data constraints. Using total capital raised to date ($180M) as a valuation proxy and applying a 2.0x step-up multiplier typical of Series A advancement yields $360M. This reflects normalized expected value creation between early and subsequent funding stages in biotech. Public-comp anchoring cannot be deployed—while the Biotech & Health sector median trades at 8.1x price-to-sales across the three public comps, Retro's revenue is not disclosed, precluding revenue multiple application. Peer-median triangulation fails due to insufficient narrow-stage comparables within the filtered set.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $306M to $414M, centered on $360M. This represents a 2.0x uplift from total capital deployed, consistent with Series A-stage biotechs in active development. Key uncertainties include the absence of disclosed revenue metrics, limiting public multiple anchoring; sparse same-stage private comparables; and stage-progression multipliers' sensitivity to company-specific technical risk, which the current dataset does not quantify.
